rules.title: Start a 5-minute task
rules.body: Cut the tasks that hold you back the most into 5-minute starter blocks, asking yourself only to open materials, write down the first step, or complete a minimal action.

rules.title: Start a 20-minute task
rules.body: Break important but non-urgent tasks into 20-minute activation units instead of asking yourself to push through them all at once.

rules.title: Record whether stage returns exist
rules.body: Observe for two consecutive weeks: Which tasks are slowing down because there is no visible stage reward, and which tasks are advancing naturally because the feedback is clear.

rules.title: Stop silently swallowing excess load
rules.body: When it becomes clear that a task, relationship, or rhythm is taking a toll on you, don't continue to keep the cost internally.

rules.title: Keep track of the types of meetings that consume you the most
rules.body: Record for two consecutive weeks: Which meetings are most likely to put you into high load early, whether it is because of vague goals, unclear responsibilities, or repeated pulling.

rules.title: Reduce the pressure of expression first, and then advance the conclusion
rules.body: When you quickly want to push a conclusion to the forefront, pause for a moment to slow down your speaking speed, turns, and space for confirmation questions before moving forward with your decision.

rules.title: Align goals first, then express objections
rules.body: Before raising objections, clarify the issues you and the other person are trying to resolve before getting into the disagreement itself.

rules.title: Condensing complexity into a decision-making problem
rules.body: Continue to use your understanding of complexity, but at the end of each discussion, wrap it up into the decision question that most needs to be answered at the moment.
